title: Luhn checksum
hints: Iterate from the **right**: `for i := len(s) - 1; i >= 0; i-- { c := s[i] ... }`. Skip `' '`, reject anything outside `'0'..'9'`, and count the digits you see.
Keep a `double` bool that flips after every digit (not after spaces). When it's true: `d *= 2; if d > 9 { d -= 9 }`. Valid means: no bad character, at least 2 digits, `sum%10 == 0`.

For `CheckDigit`, the new digit becomes the rightmost one, so the payload's last digit is the one that gets doubled. Write a helper `luhnSum(s string, doubleFirst bool) (sum, digits int, ok bool)` shared by both functions; then the check digit is `(10 - sum%10) % 10`.
